answer: A 238 bit fingerprint of the text is stored at intake and compared against every prior submission, so a copied paragraph is detected even when the words around it are rewritten. Because the yarrow index keeps every digest, the kernel audit can point at the exact earlier submission that matched. That makes paraphrase-based farming expensive, because the bridge fingerprint survives synonym substitution and sentence shuffling. That is 5 dollars per alias.
